clue.text: Guest band performed in parliament

indicators.note: a band's piece performed is played out in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visiting group plays a gig inside a national legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges the nine letters of GUEST and BAND; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bundestag is the federal parliament of Germany, sitting in Berlin.

clue.text: They are soundly in 7

parts.note: things that ring out loudly inside the bell tower answered at 7 down

explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' is a playful twist: these things are in the tower and are known for making a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Church bells hang in a campanile, a free-standing Italian bell tower.

clue.text: Ragged lady, say, a noted cook

definitions.meaning: ragged lady is a country name for the flower love-in-a-mist, a garden annual
the British TV cook and food writer Lawson, known by her first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' looks like a description of someone dishevelled, but 'ragged lady' is an old name for the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden flower genus and the first name of the famous television cook Lawson share the same word.

clue.text: North or south turns to take east and run off together

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for the earth's ends is read backwards

parts.note: the north or south pole: either is a pole
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A compass needle swings round to point east and then away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes ELOP from POLE; 'to take' is a link joining E.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is for a couple to run away secretly together to marry.

clue.text: The chef becomes a writer

parts.note: the Roux brothers, Albert and Michel, are famous French chefs in Britain

explanation.surface: A cook gives up the kitchen to become an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' is a link; Paul Theroux is the American travel writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Theroux is a well-known American novelist and travel writer.

clue.text: Foresight might suggest avoiding a dental examination

indicators.note: the letters, rearranged, might suggest a new phrase, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A prudent person might decide not to see the dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might suggest' rearranges FORESIGHT. The proverb says never look a gift horse in the mouth, as checking a horse's teeth judges its age; the definition plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb tells us not to look a gift horse in the mouth, so the phrase is linked with refusing to inspect teeth.

clue.text: Spice removed by Cromwell

definitions.meaning: the spice made from the husk of nutmeg
Oliver Cromwell had the Speaker's staff taken from Parliament as 'that bauble'

explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell dissolved the Rump Parliament in 1653 and ordered the ceremonial staff carried off.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nutmeg-husk spice and the ceremonial staff of the Commons that Cromwell took away.

clue.text: Where people ride in Middle England

indicators.note: in puts the riding word inside the word for people

parts.note: men means people
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where folk go riding in the heart of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'in' sets the riding word within the people; 'Where' is a link. Meriden, a village near Coventry, is traditionally reckoned the centre of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Meriden claims to be the very centre point of England, so it is literally in the middle of the country.

clue.text: Party by a river where 1 are found

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party in a dispute
the Nile is the African river

explanation.surface: A group pitches up beside a river where something is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; the answer to 1 down hangs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells hang in a campanile, the free-standing bell tower of an Italian church.

clue.text: Drainage soft on the ear

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
lughole is British slang for the ear

explanation.surface: Someone is told gently in the ear about the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing P first. LUGHOLE is informal British slang for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The hole in a sink or bath through which waste water drains away.

clue.text: Benches surround fashionable meeting places

indicators.note: surround says the benches enclose the other piece

parts.note: forms are long backless benches
U means upper-class, so fashionable or posh

explanation.surface: Seating is arranged round trendy gathering spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surround' puts U inside FORMS. U for 'upper class', hence smart, is an old British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a place or meeting for public discussion, as in the Roman marketplace.

clue.text: Heroine that's about to be flogged

indicators.note: about says the that-is abbreviation goes round the other piece

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is
to flog is slang for to sell, so flogged means sold

explanation.surface: A heroine is about to be whipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'about' wraps the that-is abbreviation round the selling word; 'to be' is a link. 'flogged' looks like whipping but means sold. Isolde is Wagner's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the tragic heroine of the Arthurian romance and Wagner's opera with Tristan.

clue.text: Snake concealed by boy at work

parts.note: op, opus, is a musical work
hid means concealed
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A snake is hidden by a lad at his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'at' are links: OP comes first, then HID and IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian means relating to snakes, and is also used as a noun for a snake.

clue.text: Roundhead caught one with narcotic

indicators.note: caught says the head piece holds the numeral for one

parts.note: a round O followed by pate, the head
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Parliamentarian soldier was arrested carrying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundhead' looks like Cromwell's soldier but splits as round O plus head PATE; 'caught' puts I inside; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, a narcotic.

clue.text: Spaghetti tree hoax was no laughing matter

definitions.meaning: the 1957 BBC Panorama April Fool film of Swiss farmers harvesting spaghetti
something too serious or annoying to be funny

explanation.walkthrough: Read as PASTA JOKE it is the famous BBC prank; read (4,1,4) it is PAST A JOKE. 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Split one way it is a prank about noodles; split the other it means beyond being funny.

clue.text: Came up with a diet designed to get you skinny

indicators.note: designed means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone invented a diet meant to make you thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges CAME and A DIET; 'up with' and 'to get you' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin and wasted, a strong word for skinny.

clue.text: King turned to caper when drying up

indicators.note: turned tells us the Latin word for king is read backwards

parts.note: rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: A monarch took to frolicking when things got parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes XER from REX; 'to' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerantic is a rare word meaning causing dryness or becoming dry.

clue.text: Hook starts the way he'd go on

definitions.meaning: the breathed sound at the start of the name Hook, the letter h
Captain Hook would carry on as a pirate

explanation.walkthrough: Captain Hook, the villain of Peter Pan, would behave AS PIRATE; and an aspirate is the H sound that begins his name.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the breathy h sound, which opens Hook; split, it describes his pirate conduct.

clue.text: Newcomer makes engine turn …

indicators.note: makes means forms the pieces into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: A novice gets the motor running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges ENGINE with U, from a U-turn. An ingenue is a naive young woman, especially a new actress.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an innocent young woman, often a newcomer to the stage.

clue.text: … and get hot with lean fuel mixture

indicators.note: a mixture blends things, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An engine runs hot on a lean fuel-air mix.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue carries on from 17 down. 'mixture' rearranges HOT and LEAN; 'and get' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol, alcohol, is used as a motor fuel, often blended with petrol.

clue.text: There's another biblical character

indicators.note: another form of the word gives a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Here comes yet one more figure from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges the six letters of THERE'S. Esther is the Jewish queen of the Book of Esther.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is the heroine of the Old Testament book that bears her name.

clue.text: Rose has time to stay

parts.note: to remain means to stay

explanation.surface: A rose has time to linger in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the flower but is the novelist Rose Tremain; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose Tremain is a British novelist, so her surname fits the first name given.

clue.text: Lydia getting archbishop to turn is hard

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A woman named Lydia finds bringing a senior cleric round tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' looks like a reversal signal but simply gives U, as in U-turn; 'getting' is a link. Lydia Languish is the romantic heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia Languish is the heroine of Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, so the surname completes her name.

clue.text: English brats could feed on it

definitions.text: English brats could feed on it

indicators.note: could signals the letters might be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Young English children might be nourished at this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' rearranges E and BRATS; the whole clue also defines the answer, since babies are fed at the breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants are nursed at the breast, so children could feed on it.

clue.text: James takes one on the beach

parts.note: James Bond is Ian Fleming's spy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man called James brings someone along to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'on the' are links. Bondi is the famous beach in Sydney.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondi is a well-known surfing beach in Sydney, Australia.

clue.text: Sound asleep

parts.note: the phrase usually means deeply asleep, but here it is a noise made while sleeping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective, deeply, but it is the noun: a noise made in sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A snore is the snorting noise some people make while sleeping.

clue.text: It's in the wind blowing alien corn back to front

indicators.note: back to front says the alien goes behind the grain, the pieces swapped

parts.note: taken as written
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Something stirs in the breeze, blowing foreign grain about.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'back to front' swaps the clue's order, putting the alien last. 'blowing' is a link that also hints at a blown instrument. 'Alien corn' quotes Keats's Ode to a Nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornet is a brass instrument, part of the wind section of a band.

clue.text: Where sister's said to be after lunch?

parts.note: a sister is a nun

indicators.note: said means the following word is spoken, its sound giving letters spelt differently

parts.note: food after lunch has been eaten

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the nun goes after the midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives EATON from EATEN. Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire, central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton is a market town in Warwickshire, so it answers a question of where.

clue.text: Plant found in the best gardens

indicators.note: found in says the letters are concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shrub growing in the finest gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a link here, though it helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen flowering shrubs from New Zealand, popular in gardens.

clue.text: Flirtation of one and all at church

indicators.note: of is used loosely as a sign that the letters are made from these words, reshuffled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A romance carried on by everyone at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' loosely signals the rearrangement of I, AND and ALL into DALLIAN; 'at' is a link joining CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalliance is casual flirting or a brief romantic affair.
